title: Model version lease manager and profile transactionality with dataset manifest validator
creator: Maya Chen
description: Introduce a short-lived lease concept for model-version reservations during long-running profile generation, make profile publish operations transactional to avoid partial/invalid profile artifacts, and implement a dataset manifest validator that detects prompt-to-sample mismatches before runs consume dedicated GPU capacity.
background: We frequently hit two failure modes when generating performance profiles: (1) model-version churn during long harness runs leads to partial artifacts and duplicated downstream work, and (2) dataset manifests sometimes contain prompt ids, tokenization assumptions, or sample shapes that don't match the runner contract, causing silent eval failures or wasted retrials. Both increase cost and slow model onboarding.
technical_design: High level: (a) Lease manager service: atomic lease records keyed by (model_id, model_version, harness_run_id) with TTLs, soft/force release APIs and metrics (lease_acquired, lease_expired). Coordinator will request a lease before scheduling heavy tasks and will renew periodically. (b) Transactional profile publish: harness will write candidate profile artifacts to a staging namespace (S3 prefix or internal blob store) with a manifest and checksum; a single atomic commit operation will validate checksums and move the manifest to the public profiles index. The commit is idempotent and supports rollback of partial uploads. (c) Dataset manifest validator: standalone validator that verifies declared prompt ids exist, sample payloads match prompt schemas, estimates token counts against target tokenizers (tokenizer config per runner), and runs a quick dry-run on a small sample to assert runner compatibility. Integration points: Console UI will surface lease status and staging profile previews; Console and API will reject publish attempts without active lease. Metrics: gauge for active leases, histograms for publish latency, counters for dataset-validation failures. Backwards compatibility: default to no-op for older harness versions until opt-in flag rolled out. Persistence: leases in a strongly-consistent store (etcd or DynamoDB with conditional writes), staging artifacts in existing artifact bucket with tenant-prefixed keys. Security: use existing KMS for staging artifact encryption.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge backend and validator behind feature flag. 2) Dogfood on internal models and a small set of canary customers. 3) Enable lease enforcement for new harness runs only. 4) Monitor errors and SLOs for 2 weeks. 5) Expand to all onboardings and flip feature flag. Provide fast rollback: disable lease enforcement and revert to previous publish path.
migration_steps: Run dataset-validator against the curated dataset corpus and fix top 10 manifests with highest failure rates
Backfill lease metadata for currently active harness runs by creating ephemeral leases with short TTLs
Run daily sweep to expire stale leases and reconcile any staged artifacts older than 24h
Add a one-time migration to mark existing published profiles with 'committed_at' timestamps to avoid double-commit semantics
acceptance_criteria: Leases can be acquired and renewed by the coordinator; lease metrics reported to telemetry
Staging-to-commit profile publish is atomic: either consumers see the new profile or the old one (no partial states)
Dataset validator flags schema/tokenization mismatches and prevents harness runs from starting when the manifest is invalid
End-to-end dogfood run demonstrates 30-50% reduction in orphaned/partial profile artifacts compared to baseline
No regression in 95th percentile profile generation latency beyond 10% after enabling leases
test_plan: Unit tests for lease acquisition/release and conditional writes
Integration test: harness creates lease, uploads staged artifacts, commits; assert visibility only after commit
Chaos test: simulate coordinator crash during renew and assert lease expiry and graceful reschedule
Validator test-suite with synthetic manifests exercising prompt id mismatches, schema drift, and tokenizer edge cases
Performance test: run 50 small profile generations concurrently to measure added overhead from lease checks
open_questions: Which store for leases gives the right consistency/cost tradeoffs (etcd vs DynamoDB)?
Do we require every profile publish to hold a lease or only runs using dedicated capacity?
What retry semantics should the coordinator implement for transient DynamoDB/etcd errors to avoid livelock?
comments: 2025-02-14 Maya Chen: Created ticket after incidents where two publish runs clobbered each other's artifacts. Drafted initial design.
2025-02-20 Jordan Lee: Implemented lease prototype and local integration tests. Observed ~6% overhead on microbench harness; acceptable. Pushed PR for early review.
2025-02-24 Priya Nair (PM): Reviewed rollout plan; requested additional telemetry hooks for cost accounting per-lease-hour.
2025-02-28 Security review kickoff: asked to confirm KMS usage for staging artifacts (security +dev).
